### [S029.U2] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.8 AGGREGATES FOR CONCRETE > TABLE - 10 / GRADING OF FINE AGGREGATES > NOTE - 1 For crushed stone sands, the permissible Limit on 150 micr...
- NOTE - 1 For crushed stone sands, the permissible Limit on 150 micron IS Sieve is increased to 20 percent. This does not affect the 5 percent allowance permitted in 4.5 applying to other sieve sizes.
- NOTE - 2 Fine Aggregate complying with the requirements of any grading zone in this table is suitable for concrete but the quality of concrete produced will depend upon a number of factors including proportions.
- NOTE - 3 Where concrete of high strength and good durability is required, fine aggregate conforming to any one of the four grading zones may be used, but the concrete mix should be properly

designed. As the fine aggregate grading becomes progressively finer, that is, from Grading Zones I to IV, the ratio of fine aggregate to coarse aggregate should be progressively reduced. The most suitable fine to coarse ratio to be used for any particular mix will, however, depend upon the actual grading, particle shape and surface texture of both fine and coarse aggregates.

NOTE - 4 It is recommended that fine aggregate conforming to Grading Zone IV should not be used in reinforced concrete unless tests have been made to ascertain the suitability of proposed mix proportions.

### [S048.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement > G. Fixing in position
4. Layers of bars shall be separated by precast concrete spacer blocks or spacer bars. Reinforcement shall be in correct position prior to start of concreting. No reinforcing bar shall be placed on freshly laid concrete for adjusting bar spacing. Care shall be taken to maintain reinforcement in position and keep it clean, throughout the period till it is embedded in the concrete..

### [S048.U5] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement
- I. Unacceptable materials: Reinforcement with any of the following defects shall not be permitted in the Work:
1. Bar lengths, depths, and bends exceeding specified fabrication tolerances.
2. Bends or kinks not indicated on Drawings or final Shop Drawings.
3. Bars with reduced cross-section due to excessive rusting or other causes
- J. Restore damaged bars to full capacity in a manner acceptable to the ER.

.

### [S049.U8] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
6. This design mix and trial mix hold good so long as the materials continue to be of the same quality and from the same sources. For any change, the ER may order fresh design mix and trial mixes to be carried out before the same is used at site.
7. It is the responsibility of the Contractor to prepare and get the cubes tested and to provide all the material, labour, moulds, equipment, casting and curing required.

### [S049.U9] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
8. The Contractor shall provide and maintain all the equipment and staff at the site throughout to carry out the following tests in an approved testing laboratory, hereinafter referred to as the Contractor's laboratory.
- a. Grading of coarse and fine aggregates.
- b. Silt content of sand.
- c. Moisture content of coarse and fine aggregates.

### [S049.U14] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
5. Hand-Mixed Concrete: When hand-mixed concrete is allowed and approved for certain parts of the Work, mix on watertight platforms. Proportion cement, sand and aggregate loose by volume, carefully measured. Thoroughly mix sand and cement together dry until the mixture is of uniform color. Add the aggregate and turn the

- mass over until the mixture is uniform and homogeneous. Add water by sprinkling and turn the mass over until it is uniformly mixed and of the required consistency.

### [S053.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
4. For vertical joints neat cement slurry shall be applied on the surface just before concreting. For horizontal joints, the surface shall be covered with a layer of mortar about 10 to 15 mm thick composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as the cement and sand in the concrete mix. This layer of cement slurry shall be freshly mixed and applied just before concreting.

### [S053.U5] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints
- I. Expansion Joints
1. Expansion joints shall be formed and located as detailed in the Drawings.
2. Install joint filler to allow the required dimension for sealant, as indicated. Dimensions shown on the Drawings are based on an assumed design temperature of 21 deg. C Concreting procedures shall take into account the ambient temperature range at the time of the respective operations. Do not stretch, twist, puncture, tear, or leave gaps between ends of joint fillers.

### [S053.U6] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints
- J. Waterstops:
1. Self-Expanding Strip Waterstops: Install in construction joints and at other locations as indicated, according to manufacturer's written instructions and recommendations, bonding or mechanically fastening and firmly pressing into place. Install in longest lengths practicable.
- K. Embedded Items and Inserts:
1. Accurately set anchorage devices by line and transit, and coordinate the locating of anchorage devices to be set for the accommodation of the Work of other trades.
2. Locate anchor bolts as shown on the Drawings and on shop drawings. Obtain necessary templates from the mechanical trades as required for the proper setting of anchor bolts and other items for mechanical equipment, as required.
3. Assist other trades in the installation of piping, pipe sleeves, conduit and similar items where items are to be installed in concrete. Provide frames to securely hold anchor bolts and anchorage devices in place during construction, and take care that no

### [S054.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > L. Openings
- M. Filling-In: Fill in block-outs, holes and openings left in concrete structures for passage of Work by other trades, unless otherwise shown or directed, after Work of other trades is in place. Mix, place, and cure concrete as herein specified, to blend with in-place construction. Use non-shrink materials or admixtures as appropriate. Provide other miscellaneous concrete filling shown or required to complete the Work.
